title: Дорада с сюрпризом  (Dorado with a Surprise)

segments.t: At Claude Monet, German proudly brings the dorado in salt crust to Nagiyev's table, while at Arcobaleno Viktor realizes the fish he stuffed with firecrackers for the owner was taken by Max. Let's hear the dialogue in Russian first.
Добрый вечер, Дмитрий Владимирович.
Добрый вечер. К сожалению, не знаю вашего имени.
Рита, моя сиделка из больницы.
Спасла меня от смерти и от скуки.
Это дорада в коконе фламбе.
Фламбе, я так понимаю, это гореть будет?
Конечно. Гореть будет.
Ну что ж, Герман. Сделайте нам красиво.
С удовольствием.
Какой-то гад заказал эту рыбу.
Такой план провалился.
Моя рыба готова? Забирай.
Time to unpack every phrase from the exchange you just heard.
Добрый вечер, Дмитрий Владимирович.
'Good evening, Dmitry Vladimirovich.' German uses a polite everyday Russian courtesy expression that sets the tone of the conversation right away.
Добрый вечер. К сожалению, не знаю вашего имени.
'Good evening. Unfortunately, I do not know your name.' Nagiyev uses a polite everyday Russian courtesy expression that sets the tone of the conversation right away.
Рита, моя сиделка из больницы.
'This is Rita, my nurse from the hospital.' Here Nagiyev anchors the thought on 'rita' and finishes on 'hospital', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Спасла меня от смерти и от скуки.
'She saved me from death and from boredom.' Dmitry uses the first-person pronoun in the case required by the Russian verb or preposition.
Это дорада в коконе фламбе.
'This is dorado in a cocoon flambé.' German pairs 'sea bream' with 'flambé' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
Фламбе, я так понимаю, это гореть будет?
'Flambé, as I understand it, means it is going to burn?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Nagiyev's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
Конечно. Гореть будет.
'Of course. It will burn brightly.' Here German anchors the thought on 'of course, certainly' and finishes on 'will be', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Ну что ж, Герман. Сделайте нам красиво.
'Well then, German. Make it look beautiful for us.' In everyday Russian, 'make, do' flows straight into 'beautifully' without extra linking words.
С удовольствием.
'With pleasure.' German centers this short reply on 'pleasure', letting a few direct words carry the whole meaning.
Какой-то гад заказал эту рыбу.
'Some scoundrel ordered that fish.' Notice how Russian puts 'scoundrel' and 'fish' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
Такой план провалился.
'Such a great plan fell through.' Here Chef Barinov anchors the thought on 'plan' and finishes on 'to plan', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Моя рыба готова? Забирай.

'Is my fish ready? Take it away.' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Chef Barinov's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question. Now let's replay the complete scene in Russian without interruption.

That wraps up German presenting the flambéed dorado to Nagiyev and his nurse Rita. Keep an ear out for how Russian asks for confirmation in conversation. See you next time!
